description: A three-row × four-column composite of EBSD and EDS data from Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels. Rows are labelled 15Al 525 °C × 3 h, 17Al 525 °C × 10 h and 19Al 525 °C × 10 h; columns are labelled FSD, IPF, Phase map and Mapping. Column 1 (FSD, greyscale forescatter-electron images) shows fine dark pit-like features for 15Al, a large blocky grain with internal plate-like contrast for 17Al, and elongated lath grains for 19Al. Column 2 (IPF) gives colour-coded orientation maps with an inset IPF colour key whose axis labels are unreadable: mixed red/green/blue domains for 15Al, large yellow-orange grains on a blue matrix for 17Al, green grains in a blue matrix for 19Al. Column 3 (phase maps) carries the legend β-Mn (green), BCC (red), α-Mn (blue), FCC (magenta); every row is dominated by red BCC with green β-Mn, sparse blue α-Mn and essentially no magenta FCC. Column 4 (EDS Mapping) shows 2×2 maps labelled Fe (blue), Mn (cyan), Al (red) and Cu (green). Scale bars are 10 µm for the 15Al row and 5 µm for the 17Al and 19Al rows in all four columns. Together the panels locate the β-Mn regions of the phase maps within the Mn-enriched EDS signal, supporting the caption's pairing of the α→β-Mn transformation with Mn enrichment and Al/Cu depletion.

Phase map, 10 µm scale bar, legend β-Mn (green), BCC (red), α-Mn (blue), FCC (magenta); predominantly red BCC with green β-Mn outlining regions/top-left corner and minor blue α-Mn. Legend colour bar at bottom unreadable.
2×2 EDS maps each with 10 µm scale bar, labelled Fe (blue), Mn (cyan), Al (red), Cu (green); Mn signal appears broadly uniform and Cu weakest.
Greyscale FSD image of the 17Al 525 °C × 10 h alloy, 5 µm scale bar, showing a large blocky grain with internal plate-like/lamellar contrast surrounded by a finer-textured matrix.
IPF map, 5 µm scale bar, dominated by large yellow/orange grains on a blue matrix.
Phase map, 5 µm scale bar, same four-entry legend; red BCC matrix with a large green β-Mn region occupying most of the field and little blue α-Mn.
2×2 EDS maps, 5 µm scale bars, labelled Fe (blue), Mn (cyan), Al (red), Cu (green).
Greyscale FSD image of the 19Al 525 °C × 10 h alloy, 5 µm scale bar, showing elongated, banded lath-like grains with internal streaking.
IPF map, 5 µm scale bar, showing elongated green grains on a blue matrix.
Phase map, 5 µm scale bar, red BCC matrix with elongated green β-Mn bands and few blue α-Mn regions.
2×2 EDS maps, 5 µm scale bars, labelled Fe (blue), Mn (cyan), Al (red), Cu (green).

observations.observation: The figure is a 3-row × 4-column composite arranged by alloy/aging condition in rows and by technique in columns.
The three row labels printed on the far left are '15Al 525 °C × 3 h', '17Al 525 °C × 10 h' and '19Al 525 °C × 10 h'.
The four column headers printed across the top are 'FSD', 'IPF', 'Phase map' and 'Mapping'.
The phase-map legend lists exactly four entries: β-Mn, BCC, α-Mn and FCC, colour-coded green, red, blue and magenta respectively.
Scale bars are 10 µm in the 15Al row and 5 µm in the 17Al and 19Al rows, in the FSD, IPF, phase-map and EDS panels alike.

In the 17Al and 19Al rows the phase maps are dominated by red (BCC) with large contiguous green (β-Mn) regions, whereas the 15Al phase map shows green β-Mn mainly outlining darker regions and in the top-left corner.
The EDS mapping column consists of four maps per row labelled Fe, Mn, Al and Cu, rendered in blue, cyan, red and green respectively.
The 15Al FSD image shows many small dark pit-like features, whereas the 17Al and 19Al FSD images show large blocky or elongated grains with internal plate-like contrast.

The caption states the figure contains EBSD forescatter detector (FSD) images, inverse pole figures (IPF), phase maps and EDS mapping for the 15Al (525 °C for 3 h), 17Al (525 °C for 10 h) and 19Al (525 °C for 10 h) alloys.
The citing text states that the β-Mn is rich in Mn while poor in Al and Cu, as shown in Fig. 15.
The citing text states that at 15.0 at.% Al the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within 3 h of aging at 525 °C, while the 17Al and 19Al alloys required 6 h and 10 h at 550 °C.
The citing text states that increasing Al content decreases the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn because Al enrichment around β-Mn hinders its further precipitation and growth.
